subject: maths
question: A car moves at a steady pace from point P to point Q. It would have taken an hour less if it had accelerated by 10 km/h. It would have saved an additional forty-five minutes if its speed had been increased by an additional ten kilometers per hour. How far are P and Q apart?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed 1 = S

Distance = D

Time taken at speed 1 = T

Speed 2 = S + 10 km/h

Time taken at speed 2 = T - 1 hour

Speed 3 = S + 20 km/h

Time taken at speed 3 = T - 1 hour - 45 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

LCM method for time

**Calculation:**

⇒ T = D ÷ S

⇒ T - 1 = D ÷ (S + 10)

⇒ T - 1.75 = D ÷ (S + 20)

⇒ D ÷ S - D ÷ (S + 10) = 1

⇒ D ÷ (S + 10) - D ÷ (S + 20) = 0.75

Take LCM of (S), (S + 10), and (S + 20):

⇒ LCM = S × (S + 10) × (S + 20)

Use substitution and solve:

⇒ D = 420 km

**∴ The correct answer is 420 km.**
